title: One clip, one action, one contact
rule: Give each clip a single primary action with a single contact event; split the shot if two physical events must both hold.
why: Failures cluster where several interacting events share one take; every source that lists fixes starts with fewer moving parts.
how: "She scoops soil sideways with both paws" in one clip; the covering of the hole in the next clip.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM (simple, large actions in one continuous shot)

title: Say what must stay true, as a positive sentence
rule: State the invariant in plain words ("the bottle stays open with its cap off the whole time") and put it in the prompt.
why: Models drift on state and count; naming the invariant gives the generator and the reviewer something to hold. Negation is unreliable (see phy-p-004).
how: End the prompt with a physics line: nothing appears, vanishes, multiplies or changes size; each object keeps its number.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js PHYSICS constant; src/takereview.js advice field

title: Keep the object count low and fixed
rule: Keep few distinct objects on screen and name how many ("one seed, alone on the soil").
why: Counting is a measured weakness: models almost always miss counts of nine or fewer, prompt refinement does not fix it, and similar objects merge in crowds.
how: Prefer one or two of each thing; avoid "a handful of", "several", crowds, repeated identical items.

monofilm.where: PHYSICS (one seed stays one seed); propsInClip limits props named per clip
monofilm.idea: Have the scene writer cap tracked props per clip at 3 and avoid plural counts in the clip text.

title: Do not name what must be absent
rule: Never mention an unwanted thing in the positive prompt; describe what is present instead ("deserted street", not "no people").
why: Mentioning a thing can prime it; vendors tell users to state what should happen, and Runway guidance is that negation can backfire. Where a negative field exists, use it as a list of nouns, not a sentence with "no".
how: Replace "no water, no bubbles" with the action that has none, or drop the topic; for a negative field write "wall, frame" and not "no walls".

monofilm.where: Commit f4cae7b: clip physics line no longer names bubbles, water or hands; retry drops the never-show clause and e1f1805

title: Use a negative prompt only as a targeted backup
rule: Where the model has a negative field, add a short noun list after you see a specific artifact, never as the main defence.
why: Guides agree negatives help recurring issues but are not a substitute for a good positive prompt; evidence is vendor-level and unmeasured. Some tools ignore them at low guidance.
how: Negative: "extra fingers, fused fingers, duplicate subject, flicker" only once these are observed.

monofilm.where: Generators with a negative field are not wired
monofilm.idea: Add an optional negative list per generator profile, filled from review issue kinds.

title: Avoid liquids, fire and smoke as the point of a shot
rule: Do not make a pour, splash, fire or smoke the event of a clip; show a filled glass, or show the liquid already in place.
why: Liquid transfer failed in all three of Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1 and Kling 3.0 Pro; liquids behave like gel or honey like water; PhyGenBench and Physics-IQ show fluids and state changes are weak.
how: If unavoidable: one container, one liquid action, slow gentle wording ("honey dripping slowly"), short clip, wide framing.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM: fluids only in the simplest way

title: Never let a tiny object be handled on screen
rule: Show a small object already in place and film only the large action around it.
why: Hand-object contact is imprecise, fine grasping fails and tiny items change count; fine hand contact is a stated reason to split a shot.
how: "The seed is already in the hole; she pushes soil over it" instead of "she drops the seed".

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM (a tiny object is never picked up, thrown or dropped)

title: Hands: simple poses, partial view, wide enough
rule: Choose resting, fist, or holding-an-object poses; keep hands small in frame or out of it unless the story needs them.
why: Hands fail first because of joints, overlap, occlusion and thin data; every practitioner source gives the same list. A hand flickered between four and six fingers for eight frames unnoticed in a preview.
how: "Her paws rest on the rim of the pot", mid or wide shot, steady camera, no fast gesture; one concrete pose per hand.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM (avoid fiddly paw work); takereview hands check
monofilm.idea: Add a framing rule: tiny-detail actions get a wider shot.

title: Wider framing for fine detail
rule: Frame fine detail wider and slower than feels natural, or cut the detail out of the clip.
why: Fine structure (fingers, rims, labels) is where drift shows; enlarging the prop or lowering camera movement is the repeated fix.
how: "Medium shot, static camera" while the paws work; save the close-up for a still, held moment.

monofilm.where: Not in composeClip
monofilm.idea: Pick wider default framing when the clip action involves hands or small props.

title: Slow, steady motion and a steady camera
rule: Ask for slow or steady motion and one simple camera move; name what stays still.
why: Fast or vague motion destabilises shape and limbs; flips and jumps distort joints; minimal camera motion avoids extra physics.
how: "Static subject, slow camera push-in", "slowly", "calmly".

monofilm.where: SCENES_SYSTEM (simple, large, one continuous shot)

title: Short clips, then cut
rule: Keep clips short and let the edit carry time.
why: Drift accumulates; sources cite about 3 to 5 seconds for objects, 5 to 15 for coherence; generate short and cut on action.
how: Plan a long action as 2 to 4 short clips, each ending on a stable pose that begins the next.

monofilm.where: Studio clips are short; scenes are split into clips

title: Describe weight and consequence, not just the action
rule: Add one line of physical consequence: weight, contact, what the thing does after.
why: Floaty motion appears when weight is unstated; pour tests failed with action-only prompts; a model fed steps without consequences guesses.
how: "She scoops soil sideways, small crumbs fall beside the hole and a low pile grows."

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM moves field (real physics in one or two sentences)

title: Every action must be possible at that moment
rule: Open the bottle before blowing, hold the thing before dropping it, and state the starting state of each prop.
why: Models animate the cause-effect chain they are given; an impossible start gives a wrong state or an object that appears.
how: Order the moves list: state, contact, result.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM (every action physically possible; prop named in a state only if used)

title: Do not describe what is already in the image
rule: In image-to-video, describe only the next motion; repeating the picture invites inconsistency.
why: Guide advice: describing the image reduces motion or causes inconsistencies; also add motion first, camera second.
how: Prompt: "The dog digs", not "A brown dog standing on green grass digs".

monofilm.where: composeClip uses pictures; check that it does not restate the picture

title: Review every take frame by frame, at full resolution
rule: Scan takes for count, appearance, vanishing and limbs at full resolution before accepting.
why: A six-finger flicker over eight frames was missed in a compressed preview; counts and merging are the commonest flaws.
how: Check hands, counts, edges, background shift, last frame vs the next clip.

monofilm.where: src/takereview.js (frames judged for count, physics, jump, identity, state)

title: Turn review issues into positive advice on retry
rule: Convert each detected fault into one sentence that states what must be true and add it to the next prompt.
why: Faults repeat when the prompt stays the same; model hears the invariant, not the fault. Retries also need a seed change and a cap.
how: "The bottle is open, with its cap off, the whole time."

monofilm.where: src/takereview.js advice; retry count ignores takes older than the last scene change (1c6149c)

title: Try several seeds before rewriting the prompt
rule: Generate 3 to 5 variations and pick, before reworking the prompt or the shot.
why: Sources recommend 3 to 20 variations; structural counting fixes are said to complement seed search, so luck still matters.
how: Budget 3 takes per clip and review each; stop at the cap.

monofilm.where: Studio retry loop with takereview

title: Put readable text in post, not in the generator
rule: Generate a clean blank sign and overlay text in the editor; if the story needs a sign, make a verified still first.
why: Models paint text as texture; letters drift across frames; angled signs are worst.
how: Prompt "a plain wooden sign"; add lettering in post; for in-world words make a 2K still and animate it with a slow camera.

monofilm.where: Not handled
monofilm.idea: Studio caption/title layer for text; tell the scene writer to avoid readable words on props.

title: Avoid mirrors and reflective surfaces as story elements
rule: Keep mirrors, windows and still water out of shots where the reflection matters.
why: Video models give mirrors the wrong content or layout; research is on a repair, not a prompt fix.
how: Pick another way to show a character noticing themselves, or frame the mirror edge-on.

monofilm.where: Not in SCENES_SYSTEM
monofilm.idea: Add mirrors and reflections to the avoid list.

title: Do not expect the model to know physics beyond its look
rule: Treat plausible-looking video as untrusted: check the outcome, not the smoothness.
why: Physics-IQ finds physical understanding unrelated to visual realism; case-based copying fails off distribution; VideoScience models score on coherence but not on the right phenomenon.
how: Check that the result is what physics would give (levels drop, pieces count), not only that it looks smooth.

monofilm.where: takereview prompt asks for real-life physics
monofilm.idea: Add state-change checks (levels, quantities) to the review prompt.

title: Be cautious about physics benchmark ranks
rule: Do not choose a generator by a benchmark number alone; test the physics your film needs.
why: Best models score low (VideoPhy: 39.6% on the original, VideoPhy-2 22% joint on a hard subset); results differ by category and benchmark.
how: Run a 3-clip probe of the film's riskiest physical event per generator and record it in the generator profile.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js GENERATORS

title: Use simulation or trajectories where text cannot control motion
rule: When a specific motion or impact must be right, drive it with a trajectory, a rough previs, or a simulated path.
why: PhysGen and Motion Prompting condition video on forces or point paths; a clay previs as a motion-only reference helped a pour test; sources advise hybrid production.
how: Draw a path or block with a rough animation, pass as a motion reference, keep the detail low.

monofilm.where: Not in the studio
monofilm.idea: Offer an optional motion reference or previs input.

title: Repair locally when the rest is good
rule: Fix a bad hand or region by inpainting it, and cut around what cannot be fixed.
why: Regenerating the whole shot for a small problem wastes takes; masked regeneration often needs 2 or 3 tries.
how: Mask the hand, regenerate; if it fails twice, cut away before the flaw or reframe.

monofilm.where: Not in the studio
monofilm.idea: Add a trim-before-the-flaw option in the assembly step.

title: Cut away from what the model cannot show
rule: Plan the edit so the weak event happens off screen: the beginning and the result, not the act.
why: Sources recommend hybrid and cut-on-action editing; show a filled glass instead of the pour.
how: Shot A: hand reaches; shot B: the full glass. Never the pour.

monofilm.where: SCENES_SYSTEM tiny-object rule applies this for small items
